name: unload
description: The fresh-copy unhook at breadth: compare any loaded library's mapped .text against a fresh copy and restore it -- the KnownDlls section object the preferred source, the System32 disk file the fallback the row names, the named exports alone or the whole .text -- evasion.unload's execution half packed as the artifact an implant loads through module.load.

opsec.notes: Server side, the package lands as descriptor rows and one artifact file under the module store -- no code runs in the teamserver. On the target, the implant half loads from staged task content and nothing it does lands on disk: the fresh copy is read where it sits (the KnownDlls section object preferred -- the loader's own clean copy, read through no file at all; the System32 disk file the fallback the row names) and the restore rewrites pages of the implant process's own mapping -- copy-on-write makes them private, the effect dies with the process, and a new process maps fresh libraries. The bare task is the read (the differing-byte count, whole-text or per-function); the restore is the write the operator names. The compare trusts the fresh copy only as far as a build fingerprint carries (a patch-Tuesday drift refuses). Products that guard the mapped .text (periodic re-hooking, guard-page telemetry) are a live blue-team surface -- the wider the library list and the narrower the function list, the smaller the rewrite window a re-hook needs to notice; the verb is sensitive (Evasion category, modifies-defenses attribute), held out of unattended firing by the registry-backed policy, and the plugin rides the per-engagement module load -- never a default profile.
